title: Add hook transaction log and concurrency policy for tenant installs
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: tenant installs and upgrades that use Helm init hooks can race when parallel agents attempt tenant bootstrap on the same cluster. Race leads to duplicated init work, transient DB migration conflicts, and occasional failed upgrades that require manual reconciliation. This PR introduces a hook transaction log (lightweight CR and backing ConfigMap) and a tenant-scoped concurrency policy to make init hooks idempotent and serializable across controllers.

What this PR does: 1) Adds a HookTransaction CRD and a small controller that writes a single record for each init hook execution with a deterministic hook key. The controller is intentionally simple: optimistic write with TTL and lease-style ownership to avoid long-lived locks. 2) Templates a new "concurrencyPolicy" value in the Helm chart (values.schema.json updated) that supports strategies: "serial", "per-tenant", and "best-effort". Default remains "best-effort". 3) Updates the init-job and hook templates to consult the HookTransaction API before performing stateful migrations or secret syncs. 4) Adds a tiny Terraform helper module (tenant_lock.tf) for customers who want cloud-level tenancy locks (S3/DB-based) integrated with the installer. 5) Documents the upgrade and rollback implications and provides a migration helper that backfills recent hook transactions for clusters upgrading from older chart versions.

Checklist: - [x] CRD + controller scaffold - [x] Helm templates and values/schema updates - [x] Init-job templating to check/set transaction record - [x] Terraform helper module and example usage - [x] Docs and upgrade notes - [x] Unit tests for controller reconciliation and chart linting

Why this approach: a persistent transaction record provides clear evidence that a hook ran and prevents double-run in environments where multiple controllers or human-run helm upgrades may race. The tenant-scoped concurrency policy allows operators to trade parallelism for safety. The controller is intentionally conservative: it favors correctness over subtle performance improvements.

Backward compatibility and rollout: default behavior is unchanged for customers who keep "best-effort". For tenants that opt into "per-tenant" or "serial", the controller adds coordination but does not require DB schema changes. A migration helper script is included to bootstrap recent runs into the HookTransaction store so that re-running a chart upgrade won't re-execute safe idempotent hooks.

Risks and mitigations: - Risk: controller introduces new API surface and RBAC requirements. Mitigation: default RBAC is minimal, and chart enables CRD only when values.enableHookTxLog=true. - Risk: misconfiguration may serialize installs and reduce parallel throughput. Mitigation: documented guidance and metrics to show impact; default remains unchanged.

Related: ENG-4127 (installer reliability), OPS-991 (oncall Runbook update).

discussion:
Samir Kahn: Can we avoid adding another long-lived controller? Consider a sidecar approach.
Aisha Patel: Sidecar was considered; we rejected because it ties lifecycle to job pods and doesn't provide cluster-wide visibility for multi-controller coordinations. The controller is intentionally minimal and can be scaled to run as leader-election singleton.
Ellen Brooks: RBAC looks OK but needs tighter least-privilege on ConfigMap writes.
Aisha Patel: tightened RBAC in the last commit; controller only writes annotated configmaps in the installer namespace.
Jonas Müller: request to add a metric for transaction write latency and a PromQL example.
Aisha Patel: added prometheus metric hook_tx_write_duration_seconds and a dashboard snippet to docs in the final commit.
CI: initial lint failed due to values.schema.json missing pattern; fixed in a9c5f1b. Final CI: all passing.
Merge: approved by reviewers and merged by squash on 2026-02-20.
release_notes: Added HookTransaction CRD and optional controller to serialize init hooks; new Helm value concurrencyPolicy (serial|per-tenant|best-effort) with default best-effort; Terraform helper module tenant_lock.tf for cloud-level tenancy locks; upgrade helper to backfill recent hook transactions. Default behavior unchanged unless enabled via values.enableHookTxLog or concurrencyPolicy.
summary: Introduce tenant-scoped init hook coordination via a transaction log CRD and a chart-level concurrency policy to reduce race-induced upgrade failures while preserving backwards compatibility.
notes_for_ops: Enable via values: enableHookTxLog: true and set concurrencyPolicy: per-tenant to serialize all init hooks per tenant. Monitor metric: hook_tx_write_duration_seconds and hook_transaction_total{status}. If enabling on large clusters, stage rollout tenant-by-tenant using canary label to measure throughput impact.
testing: Unit tests: controller reconciliation (success/failure/ttl-expiry), chart unit/linting; Integration: local-kind smoke test verifying single-run guarantee when two parallel installers attempt same tenant bootstrap. Automated E2E staged run on CI with mocked storage; results included under artifacts.
how_to_revert: Rollback: set values.enableHookTxLog=false and rollback chart revision; controller will stop creating new HookTransaction records but existing records remain. If run with per-tenant serial policy and rollback is required, use included migration helper to remove synthetic transaction locks created during testing.
